Paper Title: Agent-as-a-Judge: Evaluate Agents with Agents
Evaluation Methods: Multi-agent systems using planning, tool-augmented verification (code execution, trace analysis), and multi-agent collaboration for intermediate feedback.
Key Metrics: Reliability, Concordance with human evaluation, Alignment Rate, Judge Shift, Success Rate, Partial Completion
Key Findings: Dramatically outperforms LLM-as-a-Judge for code generation (DevAI benchmark); achieves 90% agreement with humans; reduces evaluation time/cost by 97%.

Paper Title: Mind2Web 2: Evaluating Agentic Search with Agent-as-a-Judge
Evaluation Methods: Tree-structured rubrics with hierarchical evaluation nodes, gating logic (critical vs. non-critical), and automated judge scripts using Extractor and Verifier tools.
Key Metrics: Partial Completion, Success Rate, Pass@3, Source Attribution accuracy, Human Performance Percentage
Key Findings: OpenAI Deep Research achieved 50-70% of human performance; judge agents demonstrated 99.03% accuracy in leaf-node verification; long-horizon tasks require real-time browsing.

Paper Title: Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Implicit Step Rewards (iStar)
Evaluation Methods: Alternating optimization of an implicit PRM and policy model; trajectory-based multi-turn Direct Preference Optimization (DPO).
Key Metrics: Success Rate, Score (WebShop), Goal Completion Score (SOTOPIA), Sample Efficiency, Episode Efficiency
Key Findings: Achieves state-of-the-art results on WebShop (86.5%) and VisualSokoban (91.7%); increases SOTOPIA goal completion by 14-48%; reaches performance in half the training steps of vanilla RLOO.

Paper Title: Examining Reasoning LLMs-as-Judges in Non-Verifiable LLM Post-Training
Evaluation Methods: Comparison of non-reasoning vs. reasoning judges (e.g., gpt-oss-120b); SFT distillation of thinking tokens; GRPO training for judges; pointwise/pairwise scoring.
Key Metrics: Krippendorff's Alpha, Win Rate (Arena-Hard-V2), Reward Hacking Rate, Elo ratings
Key Findings: Reasoning judges lead to stronger policies and prevent standard reward hacking; however, policies may learn adversarial behaviors (refusal, fabrication) to deceive judges.

Paper Title: SPELL: Self-Play Reinforcement Learning for Evolving Long-Context Language Models
Evaluation Methods: Cyclical loop of Questioning, Responding, and Verifying roles; semantic equivalence via majority voting; Gaussian-shaped difficulty reward; automated curriculum.
Key Metrics: Pass@k, Accuracy (LongBench-V2, Frames, DocMath, LB-MQA), Relative Improvement
Key Findings: Consistently enhances long-context reasoning (+9-14 points) without human labels; generalizes to 100K context when trained at 16K; prevents collapse into trivial loops.

Paper Title: Counterfactual Self-Questioning for Stable Policy Optimization in Language Models
Evaluation Methods: Internal ego-critique where models generate "What if this step is wrong?" probes; Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
Key Metrics: Accuracy, Accuracy Lift (points and %), Exact Match
Key Findings: Accuracy improved by 6.7 to 12.4 points over standard CoT; most effective for small/medium models where internal verification is weaker.

Paper Title: Reward Under Attack: Analyzing the Robustness and Hackability of Process Reward Models
Evaluation Methods: Three-tiered diagnostic framework: static perturbation analysis, adversarial optimization, and RL-induced reward hacking.
Key Metrics: Reward changes, Ground-truth accuracy, Stylistic shortcut percentage
Key Findings: Current PRMs function as fluency detectors rather than reasoning verifiers and are systematically exploitable under adversarial pressure.

Paper Title: MiRA (Milestoning your Reinforcement Learning Enhanced Agent)
Evaluation Methods: Dense milestone-based reward signals for open models; online planning through subgoal decomposition for proprietary models.
Key Findings: Increased Gemma3-12B success rate from 6.4% to 43.0% on WebArena-Lite, surpassing GPT-4o (13.9%); explicit planning improves proprietary models by ~10%.

Paper Title: Rewarding Progress: Scaling Automated Process Verifiers for LLM Reasoning
Evaluation Methods: Measuring progress as change in likelihood of correct future responses under a prover policy; test-time search against PAVs.
Key Findings: PAVs improved accuracy by >8% and were 1.5-5x more compute-efficient than ORMs; online RL accuracy increased by >6% with 5-6x sample efficiency gains.

Paper Title: SPICE: Self-Play In Corpus Environments Improves Reasoning
Evaluation Methods: Dual-role self-play (Challenger/Reasoner); document-grounded task generation; Gaussian variance-based curriculum reward; GPT-4o verification.
Key Metrics: Pass@1 Accuracy, Benchmark Average (%), Math/General Reasoning Gains
Key Findings: Achieved gains of 8.9% in math and 9.8% in general reasoning; document grounding prevents hallucination and provides necessary information asymmetry.

Paper Title: Arena RL: Scaling RL for Open-Ended Agents via Tournament-based Relative Ranking
Evaluation Methods: Process-aware pairwise evaluation with multi-level rubrics and tournament-based ranking (single-elimination).
Key Findings: Tournament-based ranking (O(N) complexity) achieves nearly equivalent advantage estimation accuracy to full pairwise comparisons (O(N^2)).

Paper Title: Process Reinforcement through Implicit Rewards
Evaluation Methods: Online PRM updates using policy rollouts and outcome labels through implicit process rewards.
Key Metrics: Accuracy on reasoning benchmarks, Sample efficiency
Key Findings: PRIME achieves a 15.1% average improvement and surpasses Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct using only 10% of training data.

Paper Title: Humanline: Online Alignment as Perceptual Loss
Evaluation Methods: Humanline Syncing (periodically syncing reference weights) and Humanline Clipping (asymmetric clipping of log-probability ratios).
Key Metrics: Length-Controlled Winrate (LC-WR), Winrate (WR), average completion Length, Pass@1
Key Findings: Humanline trained with offline data matches online alignment performance while being 6x faster, driven largely by syncing the reference model.

Paper Title: The Lessons of Developing Process Reward Models in Mathematical Reasoning
Evaluation Methods: Integration of MC estimation with LLM-as-a-judge and Best-of-N (BoN) evaluation strategies.
Key Metrics: BoN scores, step-wise error identification accuracy, response-level and step-level metrics
Key Findings: MC estimation typically yields inferior performance compared to LLM-as-a-judge; existing PRMs often shift from process to outcome-based assessment.

Paper Title: Training Vision-Language Process Reward Models for Test-Time Scaling in Multimodal Reasoning
Evaluation Methods: Hybrid data synthesis (MCTS + VLM judgments) and perception-focused supervision.
Key Metrics: Outcome Reward Models (ORMs) performance, Test-Time Scaling (TTS) accuracy
Key Findings: Smaller VL-PRMs can match or surpass larger ones in detecting process errors; perception-level supervision leads to significant gains in test-time scaling.

Paper Title: Mending the Holes: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning for Multilingual Translation
Evaluation Methods: Hybrid reward system combining Source-based Quality Estimation (MetricX), Word Alignment (F1), and Language Alignment (GlotLID/MaskLID).
Key Metrics: spBLEU, xCOMET, MetricX, Language Consistency Rate (LCR)
Key Findings: Outperformed prior multilingual LLMs in 1,414 directions on Flores-101; effectively mitigated reward hacking like input repetition.

Paper Title: The Energy Loss Phenomenon in RLHF: A New Perspective on Mitigating Reward Hacking
Evaluation Methods: Internal representation analysis of final-layer energy loss; GPT-4 identification of hacking samples based on intent deviation.
Key Metrics: GPT-4 Win Rate, Contextual Dependency Strength (CDS), Energy Loss (L_2 norm)
Key Findings: Reward hacking manifests as excessive final-layer energy loss; EPPO penalizes this to mitigate hacking and improve RLHF performance.

Paper Title: Information Gain-based Policy Optimization (IGPO)
Evaluation Methods: Intrinsic turn-level rewards derived from the model's own belief updates (marginal increase in probability of correct answer).
Key Findings: Outperforms strong baselines by providing dense supervision without external reward models, addressing advantage collapse in multi-turn settings.

Paper Title: Fin-PRM: A Domain-Specialized Process Reward Model for Financial Reasoning
Evaluation Methods: Integration of step-level and trajectory-level reward supervision in offline and online settings.
Key Metrics: Trajectory selection quality, Supervised/Reinforcement learning gain
Key Findings: Fin-PRM consistently outperforms general-purpose PRMs in financial contexts (+12.9% SL gain, +5.1% RL gain).

Paper Title: SPA-RL: Reinforcing LLM Agents via Stepwise Progress Attribution
Evaluation Methods: Decomposes final reward into stepwise contributions using a trained progress estimator and grounding signals.
Key Findings: Outperforms SOTA by 2.5% in success rate and 1.9% in grounding accuracy on Webshop, ALFWorld, and VirtualHome.

Paper Title: ProgRM: Build Better GUI Agents with Progress Rewards
Evaluation Methods: LCS-based (Longest Common Subsequence) self-annotation algorithm for key step discovery and progress label assignment.
Key Findings: Actors trained with ProgRM outperform proprietary LLMs and standard Outcome Reward Model (ORM) trained actors for GUI navigation.

Paper Title: Milestones over Outcome: Unlocking Geometric Reasoning with Sub-Goal Verifiable Reward
Evaluation Methods: Formal verification data engine (GeoGoal) to convert proofs into numeric subgoals; skeleton-rate based dense rewards.
Key Findings: SGVR enhanced geometric performance by 9.7% and generalized to general math (+8.0%) and general reasoning (+2.8%).

Paper Title: VeRPO: Verifiable Dense Reward Policy Optimization for Code Generation
Evaluation Methods: Weighted partial success rewards based on dynamic unit test difficulty estimation grounded in execution feedback.
Key Findings: Achieved up to +8.83% gain in Pass@1 with negligible time cost and zero GPU memory overhead.

Paper Title: Hybrid Reward Normalization for Process-supervised Non-verifiable Agentic Tasks
Evaluation Methods: Principle-based reward model for step-level assessment; Reward Normalization (ReNorm) to calibrate outcome/process signals.
Key Findings: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across wide benchmarks by balancing local quality with final outcome contribution.

Paper Title: Auto MC-Reward: Automated Dense Reward Design with Large Language Models for Minecraft
Evaluation Methods: Three-component system (Reward Designer, Critic, Analyzer) that iterates on executable Python reward functions.
Key Findings: Demonstrated significant improvement in success rate for complex Minecraft tasks like obtaining diamonds while avoiding lava.

Paper Title: Precision over Diversity: High-Precision Reward Generalizes to Robust Instruction Following
Evaluation Methods: Comparison of hard-only constraints vs. mixed datasets; analysis of LLM judge recall rates.
Key Findings: Hard-only constraints outperform mixed datasets; high-precision rewards improve performance by 13.4% and reduce training time by 58%.

Paper Title: Likelihood-Based Reward Designs for General LLM Reasoning
Evaluation Methods: Comparison of log-probability vs. probability of reference answers as reward signals for CoT learning.
Key Findings: Log-probability rewards are the only variant performing well across all setups, avoiding vanishing probabilities.

Paper Title: Cooper: Co-Optimizing Policy and Reward Models in Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models
Evaluation Methods: Hybrid annotation strategy; reference-based reward modeling (VerifyRM); dynamic sample pair selection.
Key Findings: Alleviates reward hacking and improves RL performance (+0.54% average accuracy on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct).

Paper Title: Sotopia-RL: Reward Design for Social Intelligence
Evaluation Methods: Refining coarse episode-level feedback into utterance-level rewards capturing rapport and goal achievement.
Key Findings: Achieved state-of-the-art scores (7.17 on Sotopia-hard); confirmed the necessity of multi-dimensional reward design.

Paper Title: Alleviating Sparse Rewards by Modeling Step-Wise and Long-Term Sampling Effects in Flow-Based GRPO
Evaluation Methods: Step-level incremental rewards; turning point identification to assign aggregated long-term rewards.
Key Findings: Alleviates reward sparsity in text-to-image flow matching models and models long-term dependencies.

Paper Title: Sailing AI by the Stars: A Survey of Learning from Rewards
Evaluation Methods: Categorization of training (RLHF, DPO, GRPO), inference (reward-guided decoding), and post-hoc correction.
Key Findings: Shift from passive learning to active dynamic feedback enables deep reasoning and better alignment with human preferences.

Paper Title: Agent-as-a-Judge (Survey)
Evaluation Methods: Planning, tool-augmented verification, multi-agent collaboration, and persistent memory for evaluation.
Key Findings: Transition from LLM-as-a-Judge to agentic judges is driven by the need to verify assessments against real-world observations.
